Roadmap¶

Planned work on VisIVO Visual Analytics, grouped by area and by horizon. Each item is a GitHub issue, where the motivation, scope and acceptance criteria are discussed; comments and contributions are welcome there.

Horizons:

  • Next: within about six months.

  • 2027: substantial work planned for 2027.

  • Long term: research items, or work that depends on external access.

The full list, with current status, is on the issue tracker and the milestones page.

Delivered¶

Items of this roadmap that are now in the software:

  • Backend health and metrics endpoints for node operation (#2): /v1/ping, /v1/node/status, /v1/metrics (The backend as an SRC node).

  • Show which node serves a dataset and fall back to the next replica (#1): the Served by column, Open via…, and the fallback to the next node when one refuses (SKAVA discovery).

SKA and SRCNet¶

Running VisIVO Visual Analytics as part of the SKA Regional Centre Network: IVOA discovery and access, node services, source finders near the data, scale.

Next

  • Benchmark out-of-core moments at SKA scale on an HPC node (#3)

  • Concurrent remote rendering sessions per backend (#4): sessions in their own processes, capped per backend and spread over the node’s GPUs; still to do: a queue above the cap, with its position shown in the client

2027

  • SRCNet sign-in through IAM (OIDC) (#6): the client signs in to an OIDC provider with configurable endpoints (tested with Keycloak); still to do against the SRCNet IAM

  • Standard SODA service on the backend, with moments and PV as remote operations (#7): sync and UWS async with OPERATION=MOMENT|PV are in place; still to do: POL, and a check with TOPCAT

  • Deploy the backend as an SRCNet node service (#8)

  • Plugin registry for source finders (SoFiA-2, PyBDSF, Aegean, photutils) (#9): the registry, SoFiA-2 and photutils are in place; PyBDSF and Aegean remain

  • Kinematic lasso: streaming connected components for very large objects (#10)

  • Kinematic lasso: multi-scale selection, 2-D edit growth and velocity conventions (#11)

  • Scaling remote 3-D rendering beyond one GPU and one node (#73), one step at a time, each measured before the next:

    • Brick pyramid for cubes, built out of core (#69)

    • Server-side out-of-core volume rendering from the brick pyramid (#70)

Long term

  • Run source finders near the data through the SRCNet Computing Broker (#12): the client submits finder jobs to a broker that follows the SRCNet job API (tested with a mock); still to do against the SRCNet broker

  • Interface for deep-learning source finders (#14)

  • Bricked level-of-detail rendering for very large cubes (#15)

  • Multi-GPU rendering of one cube on one node (#71), step 2 of #73

  • Distributed rendering of one view across nodes (#72), step 3 of #73

SKAVA¶

SKA Visual Analytics (SKAVA): finding SKA data across SRC nodes and choosing the node that should serve it, from the VisIVO Visual Analytics client.

2027

  • IVOA discovery provider: TAP ObsCore and DataLink (#5): the client queries SKAVA through TAP ObsCore and DataLink; still to do against other TAP services

Long term

  • Interactive placement advisor for SRCNet sessions (#13)

Galactic plane and multi-wavelength (ECOGAL)¶

Working across Galactic-plane surveys: aligned multi-band cutouts, compact sources and SEDs, filaments, molecular cubes and kinematics.

Next

  • VLKB service URL: one default for queries and batch cutouts (#76)

  • Open multi-wavelength cutouts of one source on a common grid (#16)

  • Cross-match compact-source catalogues across surveys in the GUI (#17)

  • Polygon and rotated-box regions for VLKB cutouts (#18)

2027

  • Multi-band aperture photometry feeding the SED fit (#19)

  • Compare SED models (#20)

  • Filament profiles and widths (#21)

  • Associate compact sources with filaments (#22)

  • Separate velocity components along the line of sight in molecular cubes (#23)

  • Kinematic distances (#24)

  • Survey coverage (MOC), per-survey colour maps and pixel values in HiPS (#25)

Long term

  • CAESAR as an extended-source finder (#26)

  • Refer to datasets by identifier instead of local path (#27)

Simulations and cosmology¶

Simulation formats, particle data at scale, flow visualisation, kinematic models and cosmology tools.

Next

  • Open a velocity field from three vx/vy/vz files in one step (#28)

  • Make the cosmology tools reachable from the GUI (#29)

  • Kinematic model: several overlays and sky position angle (#30)

2027

  • Native Gadget snapshot reader (#31)

  • Out-of-core octree for particle catalogues (#32)

  • Sparse and adaptive-mesh data in the volume renderer (#33)

  • Velocity vectors and streamlines from particle data (#34)

  • 3-D kinematic model fit with beam smearing, on large cubes (#35)

Long term

  • Non-flat cosmologies in the cosmology tools (#36)

  • Time series: light-curve viewer and dynamic-spectrum masks (#37)

Standard visualisation¶

What users expect from any astronomical viewer: linked frames, regions, scaling, publication figures, sessions, catalogues and comparison tools.

Next

  • Link 2-D image viewers: WCS match, pan/zoom, crosshair, colour scale (#38)

  • Region list: several regions, loading as editable regions, export all (#39)

  • Scale presets: zscale, asinh and percentile buttons (#40)

  • Publication figure: DPI, PDF/SVG, beam, scale bar and compass (#41)

  • WCS coordinate grid in the interactive image viewer, with ICRS (#42)

  • Spectral axis units and rest frequency in the spectrum pane (#43)

2027

  • Save and restore sessions, with undo/redo (#44)

  • RGB composite of three images (#45)

  • Line profile along a segment on 2-D images (#46)

  • Catalogue filtering, linked plots and SAMP selections (#47)

  • Compare images: blink any layers, swipe, multi-panel layout (#48)

  • Contour levels by σ, logarithmic or list, and contour export (#49)

  • Median and boxcar filters for 2-D images (#50)

  • Pixel table around the cursor (#51)

Long term

  • Python console and scripting in the GUI (#52)

Machine learning¶

Learned models that assist the user, beyond the copilot: object segmentation, source finding, similarity search, quality checks. Models propose, the user decides; data stay where they are.

Next

  • Self-hosted copilot: model default and base URL validation from the environment (#75)

  • Suggest SoFiA-2 parameters from the data (#64)

2027

  • Click-to-segment: learned object masks in cubes (#60)

  • Deep-learning source finders from the SKA Data Challenges (#61)

  • Flag anomalies and artefacts when a cube opens (#63)

  • Project and cluster catalogue columns (UMAP, t-SNE) (#65)

Long term

  • Find similar objects across archives (#62)

Cross-cutting¶

Infrastructure shared by all areas.

Next

  • Common framework for asynchronous jobs: progress, cancel, outlive the dialog (#53)

  • Asynchronous movie export with chosen resolution (#54)

  • Documentation gaps: RM synthesis and time-series data (#55)

  • Linux releases: keep the sign-in across restarts (#56): the code is in place; still to do: libsecret in the Linux release build

  • Publish a backend container image for HPC and SRC nodes (#66)

  • Contributing guide and developer onboarding (#67)

2027

  • One convention for shapes and bounds across the binary volume routes (#74)

  • Open compressed FITS directly (#57)

  • VR off the UI thread; server-side rendering on macOS and CPU-only hosts (#58)

  • Evaluate the scientific copilot (#59)

  • User study of the main analysis workflows (#68)
